labels.label: theo:CBG (statement ETT.tex:1884; gluing step: the 'inductive limit' of its proof, ETT.tex:2335-2340; Sbierski Thm 2.8 proof, glueing + point 1 Hausdorff + second countability; design package 8)

hypotheses.paper: a set of GHDs glued along pairwise MCGHDs U_ik with isometric embeddings psi_ik
hypotheses.note: any index type I (own universe), any topological spaces M i : Type u, U i j open, phi i j continuous with values in U j i; inverse continuity follows from the cocycle at k = i (phi_phi, tHomeo)

hypotheses.paper: (3.15) is an equivalence relation (transitivity from maximality of the MCGHD)
hypotheses.note: field `cocycle` in Sbierski's form is the transitivity; reflexivity from U_self, phi_self; symmetry from phi_mem together with the derived inverse law phi_phi (cocycle at k = i plus phi_self). phi_mem (phi i j lands in U j i, so with phi_phi U j i = phi i j (U i j)) encodes the symmetry of the MCGHD (U_ki = psi_ik(U_ik)), which Sbierski uses implicitly but never states; package 10 must supply it. Equivalent to mathlib MkCore's t_inter + cocycle (mem_U_of_mem)

hypotheses.paper: M~ Hausdorff from Thm 2.7 applied to pairs
hypotheses.note: proved as an equivalence t2Space_iff (T2 iff every pair gluing Gluing (val) (phi i j) is T2), no separation axiom on pieces; with T2 pieces iff every Cdist empty iff every graph closed

ADDED hypotheses: `[Countable I]` and every piece second countable (secondCountableTopology); this is not Sbierski's point 5. Sbierski's index set A is uncountable and he uses Geroch's theorem instead. This theorem does NOT cover design step 7 / package 10, whose index (SmallDev M0) is not countable in general; second countability of the maximal extension stays a geometry fact (design rem:CBG_manquant (i), DEC-49) - not this package.

hypotheses.paper: causalities of pieces agree along the gluing
hypotheses.note: CompatibleAlong = Gluing.CompatibleAlong (PushoutCausal) for every pair (i, j); shown necessary and sufficient by exists_isGluedCausality_iff; inhabited (kb/0011): compatibleAlong_ofOpens (pullbacks of one causality to open subsets glued along intersections) and compatibleAlong_const / const_timelikeLine (copies of the timelike line glued identically: absolutely minimal glued causality, every iota i a local isomorphism)

hypotheses.paper: uniqueness of the glued causality (not asserted by Sbierski; design package 10 may need it)
hypotheses.note: proved among absolutely minimal causalities only: IsGluedCausality.unique, eq_causality_of_isGluedCausality (the family analogue of LocalIsomorphism.unique, kb/0014); nothing stated without absolute minimality

findings: Sbierski's Hausdorff argument (proof of Thm 2.8, point 1) needs the map j~_ik : (M_i ⊔ M_k)/~ -> M~ to be injective, which uses that the restriction of the family relation (3.15) to M_i ⊔ M_k is the pair relation; this holds because (3.15) is already transitive (the cocycle). Formalized as injective_pair; no gap.

kb_proposals: Family gluing: mathlib's TopCat.GlueData forces one universe and bundled morphisms; CausalScaffold.CBG.FamilyGluing is MkCore's data unbundled over Σ i, M i with Quot, and its pair gluings ARE Causal.Gluing (Subtype.val) (φ i j), so every two-space Hausdorff fact transfers via the open embedding `pair`.
In a `rintro ⟨i, x⟩ ⟨j, y⟩ ⟨h, rfl⟩` on a relation written with `a.1`, `a.2`, subst fails (the projections are not reduced): `dsimp only at h e; subst e` first.

Causality.pullback along an injective continuous map reads the relations on the image (Causality.pullback_le_lt_iff_of_injective): no local-injectivity cover is needed, membership is recovered from injectivity.
